notes: The drawing room is the fireside where the household is gathered and the account must be given; the front hall beyond its double doors is the passage and threshold where cloaks, keys and carriages are waited for. The player will want to look at the sofa table where things are laid down in evidence, the fire that burns as high as it did at ten, and the coat stand and the front step where what leaves the house is decided.

rooms.name: the drawing room
rooms.description: A long room of rose-and-fawn paper and horsehair, with a white marble chimneypiece at the centre of the inner wall and two tall windows onto the snowed lawn that let in nothing but grey. A sofa table stands before the fire, a settee and three chairs about it, the Brussels carpet worn to the weave where guests have stood with their backs to the heat. The air is coal smoke and beeswax and damp wool drying. The moderator lamp on the table and the fire are the only warmth of colour in the room; everything else is winter light.

rooms.name: the front hall
rooms.description: A stone-flagged passage running from the drawing room doors to the front door, cold enough that breath shows, lit by a hanging oil lantern and whatever grey comes through the fanlight. A mahogany coat stand with brass hooks and a stick-well stands against the panelling, a single hall chair beside it, a dinner gong on its frame by the stair. It smells of wet stone, boot-blacking and the snow coming off the step outside. The front door is oak, two bolts and a chain, and the gravel sweep lies beyond it.

exits.label: out through the double doors
exits.text: The double doors give with a soft catch of brass and the cold of the flags meets you at once.
exits.back_text: You draw the double doors to behind you and the fire's heat closes over the chill of the passage.

objects.name: the sofa table
objects.description: A mahogany sofa table drawn before the fire, its leather top ringed by other winters' glasses. Whatever is laid on it is seen by everyone sitting round; that is what it is for.

objects.name: the chimneypiece
objects.description: White marble, a Carrington crest cut into the frieze, a fire that someone keeps built high. Stand at the settee and the heat reaches your face; stand at the door and it does not.

objects.name: the double doors
objects.description: Two mahogany leaves with brass finger-plates, polished where the master's hand went for twenty years and dull where a servant's would. A man standing beside them is in the room and out of it at once.

objects.name: the mantel clock
objects.description: A black marble clock under a glass dome, stopped at twenty past eleven. It has not been wound since the night, and nobody has offered to.

objects.name: the moderator lamp
objects.description: A brass oil lamp with a green shade, its chimney smoked on one side. Turned up, it throws the faces round the table into relief and leaves the corners.

objects.name: the work basket
objects.description: Miss Davenport's basket, lid open, a half-finished slipper in Berlin wool. The needle is threaded with a colour she has not used in the pattern.

objects.name: the window seat
objects.description: A cushioned seat under the east window, the velvet faded in a long oval where the master sat to watch the drive. From it the lawn is a sheet of grey with the drive a darker line, dripping now at the edges.

objects.name: the coal scuttle
objects.description: A japanned scuttle with a brass handle, filled to the lip. Somebody has made up this fire more often than the maid's rounds account for.

objects.name: the coat stand
objects.description: Mahogany, six brass hooks, a stick-well below. A gentleman's coat hung here hangs with its pockets at a woman's eye level.

objects.name: the front door
objects.description: Oak, two bolts and a chain, the lower bolt stiff with snow-swell. Through the fanlight the sweep is visible, and whether anything has turned on the gravel.

objects.name: the front step
objects.description: A worn stone step under the porch, swept twice a day and drifted over between. Boots that come in by it leave their water on the flags in a line any servant can read.

objects.name: the hall chair
objects.description: A single carved hall chair, hard oak with the crest on its back, never meant for comfort. It is where one waits for a carriage, or to be told whether one may go.

objects.name: the dinner gong
objects.description: A brass gong on a turned frame, the beater hung beside it. Fairbrother struck it at seven every night for forty years; the dent is dead centre.

objects.name: the hanging lantern
objects.description: An oil lantern on a chain, its glass fogged with cold. It makes a small warm circle on the flags and leaves the door in grey.

objects.name: the card salver
objects.description: A silver salver on the side table with the week's cards still on it, the topmost Mrs Gresham's, its corner turned down in the old way to say she called in person.
